question: What happens to a Christian who sins seriously after baptism?

answers.label: There is one repentance after baptism, and no more
The Church can reconcile every penitent sinner
Some sins the Church must not forgive

overview.text: In the second century, Hermas and the young Tertullian allowed one repentance after baptism, and only one.
Rigorists, including the later Tertullian and the followers of Novatian, refused to readmit adulterers or those who denied Christ under persecution.
The bishops chose mercy: after long penance, the lapsed were readmitted, and no dying penitent was refused communion. Trent called penance the "second plank after shipwreck".

quotes.author: Shepherd of Hermas
quotes.english: But I tell you, he said, after that great and holy calling, if anyone, tempted by the devil, sins, he has one repentance. But if he sins again and again and repents, it is of no use to such a person; he will hardly live.
quotes.original: ἀλλὰ ἐγώ σοι λέγω, φησί μετὰ τὴν κλῆσιν ἐκείνην τὴν μεγάλην καὶ σεμνὴν ἐάν τις ἐκπειρασθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου ἁμαρτήσῃ, μίαν μετάνοιαν ἔχει
quotes.context: Hermas, at Rome, announces one repentance for baptized sinners, against teachers who allowed none.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: God, foreseeing these poisons of the devil, although the door of forgiveness has been shut and bolted with the bar of baptism, has let something still stand open. He has placed in the vestibule a second repentance, to open to those who knock: but now once only, because it is already the second time; and never again, because the last was in vain.
quotes.original: Haec igitur venena eius providens deus, clausa licet ignoscentiae ianua et intinctionis sera obstructa, aliquid adhuc permisit patere. Collocavit in vestibulo paenitentiam secundam, quae pulsantibus patefaciat; sed iam semel, quia iam secundo; sed amplius nunquam, quia proxime frustra.
quotes.context: Written while Tertullian was still a Catholic.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: I hear that an edict has even been published, and a peremptory one. The supreme pontiff, that is, the bishop of bishops, decrees: "I forgive the sins of adultery and fornication to those who have done penance." What an edict!
quotes.original: audio etiam edictum esse propositum, et quidem peremptorium. pontifex scilicet maximus, quod est episcopus episcoporum, edicit: ego et moechiae et fornicationis delicta paenitentia functis dimitto. o edictum
quotes.context: Tertullian, now a Montanist, mocks a bishop (of Rome or Carthage) for readmitting adulterers.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: "But," you say, "the Church has power to forgive sins." This I acknowledge and set out even more, since I have the Paraclete himself in the new prophets saying: "The Church can forgive sin, but I will not, lest they commit others."
quotes.original: sed habet, inquis, potestatem ecclesia delicta donandi. hoc ego magis et agnosco et dispono, qui ipsum paracletum in prophetis nouis habeo dicentem: potest ecclesia donare delictum, sed non faciam, ne et alia delinquant.
quotes.context: "The new prophets" are the Montanist prophets.

quotes.author: Novatian
quotes.work: Letter 30, from the Roman clergy to Cyprian
quotes.english: Let us pray for the lapsed, that they may be raised up... When they have understood their crime, let them meanwhile be willing to show us patience... Let them knock at the doors, but certainly not break them down. Let them come to the threshold of the church, but certainly not leap over it.
quotes.original: Oremus pro lapsis ut erigantur... intellecto suo crimine velint nobis interim praestare patientiam... Pulsent sane fores, sed non utique confringant. Adeant ad limen ecclesiae, sed non utique transiliant.
quotes.context: The Roman clergy, bishop-less after Fabian's martyrdom (250), wrote to Cyprian in Novatian's hand. This is his early, moderate voice, before his schism: no hasty medicine for the lapsed, but prayer, penance and patience, not despair.

quotes.author: Cyprian of Carthage
quotes.work: Letter 57, from the council of Carthage to Cornelius
quotes.english: We had decided some time ago, dear brother, in shared counsel, that those who had been tripped up by the adversary in the persecution and had fallen and defiled themselves with forbidden sacrifices should do full penance for a long time, and if danger of sickness pressed, should receive peace at the point of death. For it was not right, nor did fatherly love and divine mercy allow, that the Church should be shut to those who knock.
quotes.original: Statueramus quidem pridem, frater carissime, participato inuicem nobiscum consilio ut qui in persecutionis infestatione subplantati ab aduersario et lapsi fuissent et sacrificiis se inlicitis maculassent, agerent diu paenitentiam plenam et si periculum infirmitatis urgueret, pacem sub ictu mortis acciperent. nec enim.. fas erat aut permittebat paterna pietas et diuina clementia ecclesiam pulsantibus cludi
quotes.context: After the persecution of Decius (250). Novatian at Rome refused to readmit the lapsed and began a rival church.

quotes.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quotes.english: If anyone dies before completing the time fixed by the canons, the kindness of the Fathers commands that he share in the holy things, and not be sent on that last long journey without provision for the way.
quotes.original: Εἰ δέ τις μὴ πληρώσας τὸν χρόνον τὸν ἐκ τῶν κανόνων ἀφωρισμένον, ἐξοδεύοι τοῦ βίου· κελεύει ἡ τῶν Πατέρων φιλανθρωπία μετασχόντα τῶν ἁγιασμάτων, μὴ κενὸν τοῦ ἐφοδίου πρὸς τὴν ἐσχάτην ἐκείνην καὶ μακρὰν ἀποδημίαν ἐκπεμφθῆναι.
quotes.context: "The Fathers" here are Nicaea (canon 13). The same letter lets a bishop shorten the years of penance for a sincere convert.

quotes.author: Augsburg Confession (Lutheran)
quotes.english: Concerning confession they teach that private absolution be retained in the churches, though enumeration of all offenses be not necessary in confession.
quotes.original: Concerning confession they teach that private absolution be retained... in the churches, though enumeration of all offenses be not necessary in confession.
quotes.context: Article 11 keeps private absolution while dropping the medieval demand to list every sin: 'Who can understand his errors?' (Psalm 19:12).

source.edition: Augsburg Confession, Article 11 (1530), as printed in Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3 (1919)

quotes.author: Augsburg Confession (Lutheran)
quotes.english: Touching repentance they teach that such as have fallen after baptism may find remission of sins at what time they are converted, whenever they come to repentance, and that the church should give absolution unto such as return to repentance. ... The Novatians are also condemned, who would not absolve such as had fallen after baptism, though they returned to repentance.
quotes.original: Touching repentance they teach that such as have fallen after baptism may find remission of sins at what time they are converted, whenever they come to repentance, and that the church should give absolution unto such as return to repentance. ... The Novatians are also condemned, who would not absolve such as had fallen after baptism, though they returned to repentance.
quotes.context: Article 12 answers Novatian's heirs directly: no fall after baptism puts a penitent sinner beyond absolution.

source.edition: Augsburg Confession, Article 12 (1530), as printed in Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3 (1919)

quotes.author: Council of Trent
quotes.english: Those who by sin have fallen from the grace of justification they received can be justified again, when, moved by God, they take care to recover the lost grace through the sacrament of penance by the merit of Christ. This way of justification is the restoration of the fallen, which the holy Fathers fittingly called the second plank after the shipwreck of lost grace.
quotes.original: Qui vero ab accepta iustificationis gratia per peccatum exciderunt, rursus iustificari poterunt, cum excitante Deo per poenitentiae sacramentum merito Christi amissam gratiam recuperare procuraverint. Hic enim iustificationis modus est lapsis reparatio, quam secundam post naufragium deperditae gratiae tabulam sancti Patres apte nuncuparunt.
quotes.context: "Second plank after shipwreck" is Jerome's phrase (Letter 130.9).

quotes.author: Westminster Assembly
quotes.english: By it, a sinner, out of the sight and sense not only of the danger, but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins, as contrary to the holy nature, and righteous law of God; and upon the apprehension of his mercy in Christ to such as are penitent, so grieves for, and hates his sins, as to turn from them all unto God, purposing and endeavoring to walk with him in all the ways of his commandments. ... As there is no sin so small, that it deserves damnation; so there is no sin so great, that it can bring damnation upon those who truly repent.
quotes.original: By it, a sinner, out of the sight and sense not only of the danger, but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins, as contrary to the holy nature, and righteous law of God; and upon the apprehension of his mercy in Christ to such as are penitent, so grieves for, and hates his sins, as to turn from them all unto God, purposing and endeavoring to walk with him in all the ways of his commandments. ... As there is no sin so small, that it deserves damnation; so there is no sin so great, that it can bring damnation upon those who truly repent.
quotes.context: The Reformed answer: repentance unto life is always open; no sin, however great, damns the truly penitent.

gaps.author: Council of Nicaea
gaps.why: Rules for receiving the Novatianists and the lapsed, and viaticum for the dying.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
